title: Large Language Models as Mirrors of Societal Moral Standards
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the alignment of LLMs with societal moral standards on various topics, including one explicitly religious topic: 'terrorism as a political, ideological or religious mean'.
findings: Models generally struggled to mirror human moral judgments on the topic of 'terrorism as a political, ideological or religious mean'. While human survey data shows strong condemnation, models like GPT-2, OPT, and Qwen2 showed a more neutral or slightly positive (acceptable) stance. The multilingual BLOOMZ-560M model showed better, more negative alignment with human judgments on this topic, though still not as strong as the survey data indicated.
references: Arnav Arora, Lucie-Aimée Kaffee, and Isabelle Augenstein. 2022. Probing pre-trained language models for cross-cultural differences in values. arXiv preprint arXiv:2203.13722.
